summary: This paper investigates coherence properties of parity-protected $\cos(2\varphi)$ qubits based on interference between Josephson elements in a superconducting loop, showing that despite suppressing single Cooper pair tunneling for energy relaxation protection, a fundamental trade-off exists between charge and flux noise dephasing. With current circuit parameters, $T_1$ exceeds milliseconds while $T_\varphi$ remains limited to microseconds, establishing practical constraints on this qubit class.
motivation: Although $\cos(2\varphi)$ qubits promise protection against energy relaxation via parity conservation, only a handful of experiments have demonstrated this protection and none have combined it with dephasing protection, motivating a comprehensive investigation of decoherence mechanisms in interference-based implementations.
method: Using numerical simulations with scQubits and QuTiP, the authors analyzed a generic SQUID model with two bi-harmonic Josephson junctions across realistic material platforms (semiconductors, superconducting circuits, heterostructures), systematically exploring how relaxation and dephasing rates depend on external flux $\delta\Phi$, junction asymmetry $d$, and the ratios $E_{J\Sigma 2}/E_{J\Sigma 1}$ and $E_{J\Sigma 2}/E_C$.
result: Optimal coherence with $E_{J\Sigma 2}/E_{J\Sigma 1}\approx-0.1$ yields $T_2\sim$ few microseconds limited by charge noise at low $E_{J\Sigma 2}/E_C$ and flux noise at high $E_{J\Sigma 2}/E_C$; even at $E_{J\Sigma 2}/E_{J\Sigma 1}=-250$ (two orders of magnitude beyond current implementations), projections reach only $T_2\sim 20$ ms, substantially below state-of-the-art transmon coherence times.
